conventions.convention: Conditional upper-tail values use the strict tail plus U times the atom; the nonrandomized value uses the inclusive tail. The conditional kernel is supplied, and U is independent of the pair (S,T).
Orbit ranks count group elements with multiplicity, rather than counting each distinct orbit point once.
Every null law in a finite-group randomization setup is invariant under every group element; the action need not be free.

Conditional rejection probabilities are supplied real integrable conditional-expectation versions. Conditional-level inequalities hold separately almost surely under each null law, without a common exceptional set.
Nuisance-freeness assumes one full-data conditional probability kernel common to the entire null subfamily, on specified standard Borel spaces with fixed realizing Polish topologies.
Fisher's example allows the common null success probability p throughout [0,1]. Its hypergeometric kernel is specified at every margin, including margins of probability zero at endpoint nulls.

load_bearing.statement: For a probability kernel K from (S,Σ) to the Borel real line, a(s,t)=K(s,(t,∞)) and b(s,t)=K(s,{t}) are product-measurable. For measurable S₀,T₀ and real U on one probability space, a(S₀,T₀), a(S₀,T₀)+b(S₀,T₀), and a(S₀,T₀)+U b(S₀,T₀) are measurable; the middle expression equals K(S₀,[T₀,∞)).

Let Y be a real random variable with CDF F and U independent of Y with the uniform Borel probability law on [0,1]. Then F(Y−)+U(F(Y)−F(Y−)) has the uniform distribution on [0,1], for arbitrary continuous, discrete, mixed, or singular laws of Y.
Under the simple null and supplied conditional law in def-randomized-conditional-p-value, for every u∈[0,1], P₀(p_U≤u | σ(S))=u almost surely, while P₀(p₀≤u | σ(S))≤u almost surely.

For a nonempty finite real list, a uniform index J, and an independent uniform U on [0,1], the strict upper rank plus U times the tied rank, divided by the list size, is uniform on [0,1]; the inclusive upper rank is superuniform.

In a finite-group randomization setup under an invariant null law, data conditional on every positive-probability orbit are uniform on its distinct points. The inclusive orbit p-value is superuniform under the null, and the independent-uniform tie-randomized value is uniform conditionally on every positive-probability orbit and unconditionally.

For a test with nonempty disjoint null and alternative parameter sets and α∈[0,1], if every null parameter has a conditional-expectation version qθ with qθ≤α almost surely, then Eθφ(X)≤α for every null parameter, and the test has size at most α.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 establishes a conditional law Λ_S of (T,U) through identities for fixed product-Borel events. Step 2.1 then concludes conditional uniformity for p_U, whose defining transformation depends on S itself. The required passage to the S-dependent event { (t,v): K(s,(t,∞))+vK(s,{t})≤u } is not explicitly justified by those fixed-event identities. A short additional rectangle/Dynkin argument closes this gap. Alternatively, the opened existing item lem-regular-conditional-kernels-push-forward-under-measurable-random-maps supplies exactly this passage; combine it with the batch's tail/atom measurability lemma and cite it as a dependency. The claimed uniformity remains mathematically sound.
